context.guidance: Serve every route that carries Personal Data over TLS only, and set Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite attributes on session cookies. Replace wildcard cross-origin rules with an explicit list of trusted origins. These transport and session controls are part of the safeguards Rule 6(1)(a) requires for the Personal Data they carry.

value.fix: Change `res.jsonp(response)` to `res.json(response)` and turn off JSONP callbacks across the app with `app.disable('jsonp callback name')`, or simply never call `res.jsonp`. JSONP sends the Personal Data as a script, and any site can load a script, so this acts like a wildcard cross-origin rule that skips CORS. If another origin really needs this data, use the `cors` middleware with a fixed list of trusted origins, for example `cors({ origin: ['https://app.example.com'], credentials: true })`. Don't use `*` and don't echo back the request's Origin header. Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` so browsers can't run the JSON as a script. Serve this route over HTTPS only: redirect HTTP to HTTPS, set an HSTS header, and set `app.set('trust proxy', 1)` if the app sits behind a proxy. Set the session cookie with `{ secure: true, httpOnly: true, sameSite: 'strict' }`, or `'lax'` if cross-site navigation must keep working. This closes the cross-origin read path and supports the Rule 6(1)(a) safeguards for this Personal Data.
